summary: Edward Denison Ross (1871-1940) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied at University College London, later chairing Persian there, serving at the British Museum, and heading SOAS University of London.

Edward Elbridge Salisbury (1814-1901) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Yale, and in Europe under Woolsey, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Burnouf, Bopp, and Lassen. He served as professor at Yale and secretary of the American Oriental Society.
Edward Espe Brown (1945-) is an active scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki from around 1966 to 1971, as well as under traditional teachers Reb Anderson and Jack Kornfield.

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell and held an academic post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett (1971-) specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at UCLA under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, completed postdoctoral training with Anna Szabolcsi, and worked at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Granville Browne (1862-1926) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge, and served as the Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from around 1902 to 1926.
Edward H. Schafer (1913-1991) was a Sinologist. He studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University. From around 1947 to 1984, he served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Edward James Rapson (1861-1937) was an Indologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he worked at the British Museum and University College London before becoming professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge from around 1906 to 1936.

Edward Joseph Thomas (1869-1958) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews, served at the Cambridge University Library from roughly 1910 to 1939, and held a professorship at the University of Cambridge.

Edward Washburn Hopkins (1857-1932) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Columbia and Leipzig under Weber and Windisch, he held posts at Columbia, Bryn Mawr, and Yale, where he served as professor from 1895 to 1926.

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lobsang, Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and was a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University.
Edwin Arnold (1832-1904) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. His education included studies at the King's School, Rochester, King's College London, and University College, Oxford.

Edwin F. Bryant (1957-) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University and held appointments at Harvard University and Rutgers University, where he became Associate Professor of Hinduism around 2003.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson (1840-1890) was an Indologist and historian educated at Trinity College Dublin. He served as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal and as President of the Asiatic Society from around 1886 to 1888.
Edwin Gerow (1931-) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College and was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society.

Edwin Whitfield Fay (1865-1920) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins under Bloomfield, Gildersleeve, Wright, Smyth, Warren, and Bright, holding posts at the University of Michigan and Washington and Lee University.

Egaku Maeda (1926-2010) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Meijo University and served as professor at Aichi Gakuin University from approximately 1974 to 1997.
Eiichi Yamaguchi works in Indology and philosophy. He completed his graduate studies at Kyushu University and served there as a research assistant in 1991.

Eiki Hoshino (1943-) works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University from roughly 1963 to 1970 and later served there as a professor and director in the Faculty of Humanities.

Eisaku Okada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University and held appointments at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Koyasan University, and Kyoto University.
